prompt: I wired up a ScrubStage with our new hero clip, and it plays fine when I scrub the video player directly, but on the actual page the pinned scene just holds the first frame the whole way down and only jumps to the last frame right at the bottom. The pin geometry and --fluid units all look correct in devtools.
expected_output: Diagnoses a non-all-intra (long-GOP) encode, not a scrub/pin bug — a scrubbed video needs to seek to an arbitrary frame every rAF, and a long-GOP clip can only seek cleanly to its I-frames, so every seek in between decodes from the nearest prior keyframe and reads as stuck-then-jump. Points at the all-intra re-encode (ffmpeg -g 1) and does not propose editing ScrubStage's progress/pin math.

assertions.text: identifies a non-all-intra / long-GOP encode as the cause, not the pin or scroll math
assertions.check: response mentions all-intra/keyframe/GOP as the cause

assertions.text: gives the ffmpeg re-encode fix (-g 1 or equivalent all-intra flag)
assertions.check: response contains an ffmpeg command with -g 1 or -x264-params keyint=1

assertions.text: does not propose editing ScrubStage's scroll/progress math as the fix
assertions.check: no code edit to ScrubStage's progress or rAF logic suggested as the fix

assertions.text: explains why an arbitrary-frame seek needs every frame to be a keyframe

prompt: We have an existing marketing site on GSAP with ScrollTrigger timelines all over it, and Lenis for smooth scroll. I want to add one new ScrubStage hero and a PullToCentre section without breaking any of the existing GSAP animations or the Lenis smooth scroll everywhere else.
expected_output: Asks (or states the default) keep/adapt/replace for the existing GSAP timelines and Lenis rather than assuming a rip-and-replace; recommends keeping Lenis site-wide but disabling it (or suspending it) over the new scroll well's range, since Lenis and the well are both scroll-position writers; keeps the new ScrubStage's pin as CSS position: sticky and explicitly does not nest it inside a GSAP ScrollTrigger pin: true; calls ScrollTrigger.refresh() after the new section's layout is measured.

assertions.text: surfaces the keep/adapt/replace choice for existing GSAP timelines and Lenis instead of silently replacing them
assertions.check: response asks or states keep/adapt/replace for existing motion

assertions.text: recommends disabling or suspending Lenis over the scroll well's range, not running both unmodified
assertions.check: response mentions disabling/suspending Lenis or routing through lenis.scrollTo for the well

assertions.text: keeps ScrubStage's pin as CSS sticky, not a GSAP ScrollTrigger pin
assertions.check: response does not wrap ScrubStage in pin: true

assertions.text: mentions ScrollTrigger.refresh() after adding the new section

prompt: Our fixed header is supposed to switch to light text over dark sections and dark text over light sections as you scroll, but right now it stays dark the whole way down, even when it's sitting on top of our dark stats band.
expected_output: Checks that every section (including the dark stats band) carries data-header-theme, diagnoses a missing or misspelled attribute on the offending section rather than a bug in the probe/hook itself, and explains the probe reads the section currently under the header (not the one in view), so a section with no attribute silently falls through to whatever the last resolved value was.

assertions.text: checks/asks whether the dark stats band carries data-header-theme="dark"
assertions.check: response checks for or mentions data-header-theme on the dark section

assertions.text: diagnoses a missing/misspelled attribute on the section, not a bug in useHeaderTheme/headerTheme.ts itself
assertions.check: response identifies a missing or wrong data-header-theme value as the cause

assertions.text: explains the probe reads whichever section is currently under the header, and a section with no attribute falls through to the last resolved value
assertions.check: response explains the under-header probe / fall-through behaviour

prompt: Our site uses the fluid-design scale. I added a GSAP ScrollTrigger so the hero bottle slides 600px to the right as you scroll (x: 600, end: '+=1200'), and it looks right on my 1440 laptop but on the 27-inch iMac it only moves a bit and stops too early. The bottle also has an entrance animation and I centred it with lg:fluid-translate-x-[-50%]... What's wrong?
expected_output: Explains that drawn travel must scale on a fluid layout (1.6x at 2560x1440); rewrites with fluidValue(600)/fluidEnd(1200) and invalidateOnRefresh, or the --scene-p CSS pattern; warns that GSAP folds CSS translate into its transform on elements it tweens, so the drift/any calc translate goes on a child or wrapper (a pure % centring survives); mentions audit-motion's fixed-travel-on-fluid rule.

assertions.text: identifies fixed px travel as the cause
assertions.check: response says x: 600 / end '+=1200' do not scale
response contains fluidValue or fluidEnd or --scene-p

assertions.text: sets invalidateOnRefresh when using function values
warns about GSAP folding translate on the tweened element
assertions.check: response mentions GSAP folding translate / putting the offset on a child or wrapper
